criteria.criterion: Separates the fixed requirement from the execution strategy
criteria.evidence: The whole plan treats the 3-week deadline as given and builds the execution around it (canary, rolling batches, a week of buffer). It never says outright that the requirement is fixed and only the execution can vary. It also softens the requirement: "Ask security for risk-based ordering... in case you can't finish everything."

It explicitly declines to collect criticality: "You can't classify criticality reliably, so don't try to guess... Live-migrate by default." It asks owners for input only on non-migratable VMs ("notify the project owner and let them choose a slot"). There is no shared table of consumer-provided criticality required before execution.

criteria.criterion: Computes or frames capacity per availability zone
criteria.evidence: "roughly 2 to 3 per AZ. You'll need to confirm the real per-AZ figure, because it sets the batch size"; "Run 2 hosts per AZ at a time"; "Pull per-AZ free capacity and check that each AZ can really absorb a batch."

criteria.criterion: Handles SR-IOV instances by release: live migration with a brief interface interruption (owner agreement) where supported, restart or cold migration otherwise
criteria.evidence: "Check whether your Nova, libvirt and NIC combination supports live migration with SR-IOV ports... If it doesn't work, assume cold migration or stop/start." This makes the decision depend on version. It does not mention Train, the brief interface interruption that needs owner agreement, or the difference from flavor-based PCI passthrough. It also groups "SR-IOV, GPU, pinned or otherwise non-migratable" together in the classification.

criteria.criterion: Explains landing zone and version direction constraint
criteria.evidence: Landing zone is covered: "Patch the empty buffer hosts first. Drain the next batch onto them." The constraint against migrating from newer to older QEMU/libvirt is never stated.

criteria.criterion: States that running instances are only protected after migration or restart
criteria.evidence: "The QEMU fix only applies to a VM when its QEMU process restarts. Live-migrating a VM onto an already-patched host gives it the new QEMU."

criteria.criterion: Defines stop conditions and completion criteria
criteria.evidence: Stop condition: "stop the pipeline if a batch has more than N failed migrations or hosts that don't come back." There are no campaign completion criteria (for example, every instance migrated or restarted onto patched QEMU). There is only a daily burn-down to track.

criteria.criterion: Does not recommend evacuation for maintenance
criteria.evidence: Evacuation is never suggested. Hosts are drained by live migration, or by cold migration or stop/start for VMs that can't be live-migrated.

critical_errors.error: plans to live-migrate everything despite insufficient capacity
critical_errors.evidence: Uses a rolling 'leapfrog' plan with 2 hosts per AZ in flight and reserve kept back. It does not try to migrate everything at once.

critical_errors.error: restarts workloads without owner input on criticality
critical_errors.evidence: For non-migratable and SR-IOV VMs it notifies owners and lets them choose a slot or move the VMs themselves before a deadline. It falls back to "Whatever they haven't moved by the deadline gets moved by you" only after notice. This is borderline, but owners do get a chance to give input.

critical_errors.error: treats patched hosts as protecting running instances that were not migrated or restarted
critical_errors.evidence: States plainly that the QEMU fix applies only once the QEMU process restarts or the VM migrates.

critical_errors.error: classes all SR-IOV instances as requiring a restart without considering the release
critical_errors.evidence: "Check whether your Nova, libvirt and NIC combination supports live migration with SR-IOV ports... Support depends on version and NIC."

critical_errors.error: invents capacity numbers per AZ and presents them as known
critical_errors.evidence: "roughly 2 to 3 per AZ" is presented as an estimate based on an even split, with "You'll need to confirm the real per-AZ figure."

summary: A solid, practical rolling-patch plan. It frames capacity per AZ, patches landing-zone hosts first, states correctly that running VMs are protected only after migration or restart, avoids evacuation, and ties SR-IOV handling to the release. It falls short of the expected reasoning in several places. It explicitly declines to collect consumer criticality up front instead of requiring a shared criticality table. It omits the rule against migrating from newer to older QEMU/libvirt. It does not mention the brief SR-IOV interface interruption that needs owner agreement, or the difference from PCI passthrough. It defines stop conditions but no campaign completion criteria. It commits none of the critical errors.
